overview: Apple's June quarter revenue rose 16% to a record $109.4B, with iPhone up 22% to $54.3B and Mac up 29% to $10.4B despite supply constraints; diluted EPS rose 29% to $2.02 including $0.11 of tariff refunds. Kevan Parekh, CFO, guided September revenue growth to 9%-11%, down from the 14%-17% June guide, on a roughly 2.5-point FX headwind and supply constraints expected to increase significantly. Tim Cook, CEO, said this was his final earnings call.
keyTakeaways: Tim Cook, CEO, blamed the advanced-node SoC constraint on demand running ahead of forecast, not suppliers, with constraints broadening from Mac to iPhone, Mac and iPad in September.
Cook said Apple reluctantly raised iPad and Mac prices amid a "100-year flood" in memory pricing, with costs higher again in September.
Services growth slowed from 16% to 12%, which Kevan Parekh, CFO, attributed mainly to FX plus the F1 compare, mobile gaming softness and the U.S. link-out ruling.
Siri AI arrives this fall; Cook said Apple has no complete plan yet for recovering compute costs beyond iCloud+ upgrade tiers, and cannot yet launch it on iPhone and iPad in the EU.
financialHighlights: Revenue $109.4B (+16%) with June quarter records in every geographic segment; products $78.7B (+18%), services $30.7B (+12%).
iPhone $54.3B (+22%), Mac $10.4B (+29%), iPad $6.2B (-6% on the A16 iPad compare), Wearables $7.9B (+6%).
Gross margin 50.1% including about 2 points of tariff refunds; 48.1% excluding them versus 49.3% in March, a decline Parekh said memory costs more than explain.
Net income $29.8B, EPS $2.02 and operating cash flow $34.4B were June quarter records even excluding refunds; OpEx $19.1B (+23%); $33B returned to shareholders.
guidance: Kevan Parekh, CFO, expects September revenue growth of 9%-11% (June guide 14%-17%), with FX a roughly 2.5-point sequential headwind and constraints across iPhone, Mac and iPad.
Parekh expects mid-teens iPhone growth and services growth similar to June's 12% after a further 2.5-point FX headwind.
Parekh guided gross margin to 47%-48% including about 1 point of tariff refunds (46.5% ex-refund versus 48.1%), the decline more than explained by memory.
Parekh guided OpEx to $19.1B-$19.4B, OI&E around $350M and tax around 16.5%; no color beyond September.
risksMentioned: Supply constraints on advanced-node SoCs, which Tim Cook, CEO, called "very significant" with limited flexibility to remedy.
Memory costs rising again in September and, per Cook, continuing to increase beyond it as the carry-in inventory offset shrinks.
FX: about 2.5 points sequential on total growth and about 5 points cumulative on services from March to September, per Kevan Parekh, CFO.
App Store headwinds from mobile gaming, business model changes and the U.S. link-out ruling; unknown price elasticity; Siri AI regulatory delays in the EU and China.

qa.question: How much of the roughly 500 bps September deceleration is supply versus FX, and why are constraints broadening?
qa.answer: FX is a roughly 2.5-point sequential headwind and supply constraints increase significantly across iPhone, Mac and iPad, together bridging to June's growth. Tim Cook, CEO: memory costs rose significantly from March to June, will be higher in September, and the carry-in offset shrinks after that.

qa.question: How much do supply constraints hit the December quarter, and could Apple broaden its silicon suppliers?
qa.answer: The root cause is a demand forecast miss, with iPhone up 22% and Mac up 29%, and September will be "scrambling on the supply side"; Parekh gave no guidance beyond September. Cook: "this isn't a partner or supplier issue"; Apple sources over 100M Arizona components this year.
qa.read: Declined to quantify December; pushed back on supplier premise.

qa.question: Will Apple pursue multi-year supplier LTAs, protect gross profit dollars or margins, and why did services decelerate?
qa.answer: Pricing weighs units, revenue and margin over the long term, not a 90-day clock; LTAs went unaddressed. Parekh: services fell from 16% to 12% mainly on FX, plus the F1 compare, mobile gaming and the link-out ruling.

qa.question: Where does Siri AI stand in China and Europe, and how much of the gross margin decline is FX versus commodities?
qa.answer: Apple is working with the EU commission and offers Siri AI on Mac there; China approved original Apple Intelligence features last week. Parekh: the 120 bps drop to 48.1% and the 160 bps drop to 46.5% are each more than explained by memory, with FX "a pretty minimal impact".

unanswered.question: How much do supply constraints hit the December quarter?
unanswered.how: Kevan Parekh, CFO: "Beyond September, we're not providing any color at this point."

unanswered.question: What adoption does Apple expect for Apple Upgrade, and will it shorten the replacement cycle?
unanswered.how: Tim Cook, CEO, said uptake remains to be seen; no figures given.

unanswered.question: How is the competitive landscape changing with potential OpenAI or SpaceX AI devices?
unanswered.how: John Ternus, incoming CEO, said Apple is focused on its own plans; no comment on competitors.
